19 An extension–force graph for a spring is shown.
15
extension / cm
0
0
6.0
force / N
What is the spring constant of the spring?
A
0.025 N m–1
B
0.40 N m–1
C
2.5 N m–1
D
40 N m–1

hints: Notice the graph has extension in $\text{cm}$ on the vertical axis and force in $\text{N}$ on the horizontal axis, reaching $15\text{ cm}$ at $6.0\text{ N}$.
Recall Hooke's law $F = kx$, so $k = F/x$ and $k$ must be in $\text{N m}^{-1}$, which means the $15\text{ cm}$ extension must be converted to metres.
Calculate $6.0$ divided by $0.15$ and check why dividing by $15$ or dividing $0.15$ by $6.0$ gives the distractor values.
walkthrough: Read the end point of the straight line through the origin: a force of $6.0\text{ N}$ produces an extension of $15\text{ cm}$.
State the governing relation for a spring obeying Hooke's law: $F = kx$, rearranged to $k = F/x$.
Convert the extension to SI units for $k$ in $\text{N m}^{-1}$: $x = 15\text{ cm} = 0.15\text{ m}$.
Substitute the values: $k = 6.0/0.15 = 40$ and check units as $\text{N}/\text{m} = \text{N m}^{-1}$.
The value $40\text{ N m}^{-1}$ matches the calculated spring constant. This is option D

A.explanation: This is $x/F = 0.15/6.0 = 0.025$ with units inverted, giving compliance not spring constant.

B.explanation: This is $6.0/15 = 0.40$ using extension in $\text{cm}$, missing the conversion to $\text{m}$ for $k$ in $\text{N m}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This is $15/6.0 = 2.5$, which is extension divided by force with no unit conversion, the inverse of $k$ in mixed units.

D.explanation: With $F = 6.0\text{ N}$ and $x = 0.15\text{ m}$, $k = F/x = 40\text{ N m}^{-1}$.
